clue.text: Ghost, first to last, in Hell

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is moved to the end, rotating the word round by one place

parts.note: a shade is a ghost or spirit of the dead

explanation.surface: A spirit pushed from the front of the queue to the back in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: SHADE with its S moved from the front to the back gives HADES.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is the underworld where the souls of the dead dwell, used loosely for the infernal regions.

clue.text: Study of waterworks beginning to help lady's uric failing

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only, so just that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of help

indicators.note: something failing has broken down, so these words are taken apart and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding report on a woman's ailing urinary system, framed as a study of her waterworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterworks' is slang for the bladder, which suits the uric surface, but the definition means the engineering of flowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydraulics is the branch of engineering concerned with fluids in motion, such as pipes, pumps and water supply.

clue.text: Two fairish holes, say, by end of work help to block the road

parts.note: a double is two of something
par is the standard score for golf holes, and 'par' also means average or fairish

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of work

explanation.surface: A golfer's middling round followed by roadworks that obstruct traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture hides the motoring answer: a double par is a poor score, and the K closes it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-park is to leave a car alongside another parked vehicle, obstructing the carriageway for passing traffic.

clue.text: Paid tribute to having the blues involving stringed instrument

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: having the blues means feeling sad
the lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A melancholy musician honouring someone with a mournful tune on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to honour or acknowledge them formally, so saluted is the past tense of paying tribute.

clue.text: Ruler's adapted Roman style

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered to fit, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
chic is stylishness or elegance

explanation.surface: An emperor's taste adapted from classical Roman fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchic describes things belonging to a monarch, so it works as the possessive adjective for a sovereign or king.

clue.text: Church music is covered by simple scripture lesson

indicators.note: something covered by another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than
taken as written
RE is Religious Education, the school scripture lesson

explanation.surface: Choral music being folded into a plain Sunday-school Bible lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, Religious Education, is the standard crossword scripture lesson; 'simple' here means nothing more than.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miserere is a setting of Psalm 51, sung in church, famously by Allegri for the Sistine Chapel.

clue.text: Scottish one engaging detective showing rise in distinction

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads from bottom to top, so the letters are turned around
engaging means taking in or holding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: yin is the Scots word for one
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A Scot hiring a private investigator and so climbing socially.
explanation.walkthrough: Yin is the Scots form of one; 'rise' only works because this is a down entry, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine point or subtle difference, the same as a fine distinction between things.

clue.text: Are bubbling pan and casserole finally getting stirred again?

indicators.note: something bubbling is churning about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a wok is a Chinese cooking pan

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of casserole

explanation.surface: A cook checking whether the pots on the hob are being stirred again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirred' looks like kitchen stirring but means woken.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to wake from sleep, so stirred again means woke up a second time.

clue.text: See 9
Irish city's two-word reinterpretation of shamrock?

indicators.note: a sham is a fake, so the word after it is a counterfeit version, its letters rearranged

parts.note: read as two words, sham and rock; the second is taken as written

explanation.surface: An Irish city's own playful take on the national emblem, the shamrock.
explanation.walkthrough: Read shamrock as two words, 'sham rock': sham signals a rearrangement of ROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is the second-largest city in the Republic of Ireland, in the south of the country.

clue.text: What could make House go mad, involving Liberal politician of the past

indicators.note: the answer is what the following letters could be made into once they are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Speculation about a past politician who could drive the House of Commons to madness, with a Liberal involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go mad' reads as part of the indicator but its letters are fodder too: all of HOUSE GO MAD plus L are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec Douglas-Home was a Conservative prime minister in 1963 to 1964, a statesman of an earlier era.

clue.text: Religious reformer organised millions in church, right?

indicators.note: the words before sit inside the church abbreviation that follows

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to run something is to organise it
M is the abbreviation for millions
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A churchman reorganising the finances and putting millions into the church, asking if that was right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is a plain synonym in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Cranmer, Archbishop of Canterbury under Henry VIII, led the English Reformation and wrote the Book of Common Prayer.

clue.text: Term to typify "Troubled toenail trial"?

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so the letters of the words after it are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Seeking the right literary term for a tongue-twister about a painful foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: three words all starting with T are an example of the device, and the last two words rearrange into its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliteration is the repetition of the same initial consonant sound in neighbouring words, as with the three Ts here.

clue.text: They weigh horses, restraining flanks of lively Arab

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the first piece wraps round what follows

parts.note: steeds are horses

indicators.note: the flanks of a word are its two sides, the outer letters only

parts.note: the first and last letters of lively
AR is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A description of thoroughbred horses being held back by a lively Arab stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They weigh' sounds like it belongs to the horses, but steelyards are weighing devices.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is a balance with a sliding counterweight on an arm, used for weighing goods.

clue.text: Patriot's worship given to Biblical figure

parts.note: Paul the apostle, author of many New Testament letters
to revere is to worship or venerate

explanation.surface: A patriot's devotion being transferred to a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given to' places the worship after the Biblical figure; 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere was an American revolutionary famed for his midnight ride warning of the British advance in 1775.

clue.text: Like memorial words daughter inscribed in large beehive?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: something inscribed in a thing is written within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an apiary is a place where bees are kept
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter's tribute carved into an oversized beehive, an odd memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside L plus APIARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapidary describes language suited to an inscription in stone: concise, elegant and dignified, as on a monument.

clue.text: Big user of ammo, live — artillerymen accepting that (not half)

indicators.note: not half means only half survives, the other half of the word being dropped

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the gunners' letters wrap round what follows

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
the first half of that

explanation.surface: Gunners taking in a giant weapon that gets through plenty of ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Bertha was a huge German howitzer of the First World War, named for Bertha Krupp; the clue's 'Big' leads to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Bertha was the nickname of an enormous German siege howitzer that fired massive shells, a voracious consumer of ammunition.

clue.text: Gold metal picked up with information indicating another element

indicators.note: in a down clue something picked up is lifted from the bottom upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
tin is a metal
gen is slang for information

explanation.surface: Chemistry notes about gold and another metal pointing to a further element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' works because gold and tin are elements too.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a chemical element, the colourless gas that makes up most of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Character, fashionable? That's fashion guru

parts.note: a card is a character, an amusing eccentric
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Asking whether a stylish personality counts as a fashion leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Cardin was a French couturier whose label and futuristic designs made him a leading figure in fashion.

clue.text: Here's me behind the times, showing inability to move forward

parts.note: here's me becomes I'm, the speaker saying 'I am'
passé means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they are out of date and stuck in a rut.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a situation where no progress is possible, so it is the state of being unable to advance.

clue.text: Girl's lines added to exercise put down wrongly

parts.note: a miss is a girl
PE is physical education
L is for line, so two Ls are lines

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl given lines on top of her gym lesson as punishment for a wrong answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' is the school punishment in the surface, but in the wordplay each line is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: To misspell is to write a word down incorrectly, getting its letters wrong.

clue.text: Plan in school making a mark

indicators.note: one word sits inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
a plot is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A school scheme for earning a good grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a grade in this school setting but is a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A splotch is a large irregular stain or blot, a mark smeared or spattered on something.

clue.text: Plan in school: English supported by the writer

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
E is the abbreviation for English
the writer is the setter, referring to himself as me

explanation.surface: A teacher's English syllabus, backed up by the author of the textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supported by' puts the writer underneath, so ME comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan or arrangement for doing something.

clue.text: How star's seen — touring pretty places?

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the letters go on the move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity spotted on a tour of scenic beauty spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity touring, but it is an astronomical star.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers classify each star by the features of its light spectrum, such as O, B, A, G or M classes.

clue.text: Southern gents possibly doing for East European

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the gents is a men's toilet, one kind of lav

explanation.surface: Men from the south possibly passing themselves off as East Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: The gents is the British name for a men's public toilet; lav is short for lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavs are the peoples of eastern and central Europe speaking Slavic languages, such as Poles, Czechs and Russians.

clue.text: Bridge system, all but nearby to the North

indicators.note: in a down clue going to the north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
all but means everything except the very last part, so the final letter goes

parts.note: local means nearby

explanation.surface: A road map of bridges in the area, almost all lying to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCAL loses its last letter to give LOCA, then reads upwards. Acol is a bidding system in the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Acol is the standard bidding method in British contract bridge, named after the Acol Road club in London.

clue.text: Company's acquired by recently successful tennis player

indicators.note: something acquired by another thing is taken into it, so it goes inside

parts.note: late means recently, as in 'of late'
CO is the abbreviation for company, plus the S

explanation.surface: A firm being bought up by a tennis player who has lately been winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recently successful' reads as one phrase, but 'recently' is the wordplay and 'successful' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: René Lacoste won seven Grand Slam singles titles in the 1920s and later founded the clothing brand with the crocodile logo.

clue.text: Theatrical director, instinctive, to move quickly to secure run

parts.note: a gut reaction is instinctive

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the word before wraps round the next

parts.note: hie is an old word meaning hasten
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A director with good instincts hurrying to lock in a long theatrical run.
explanation.walkthrough: Hie is an archaic verb still common in crosswords; 'run' suggests a show's run but is the single letter from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Tyrone Guthrie was a celebrated British stage director who founded the Stratford Festival in Canada.

clue.text: Very like some fairies to cover shirt in soft fabric

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so the fairy word wraps the shirt word

parts.note: elves are fairies, so elven means like them
a tee is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: Fairy-like folk wrapping a shirt in a soft cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The tee shirt sits near the end of the fairy word, between its fourth letter and the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Velveteen is a cotton fabric with a short dense pile imitating velvet, so it is soft to the touch.

clue.text: German writer pinches several bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the words before it contain the answer within them

parts.note: sits inside these two words

explanation.surface: A German author helping himself to a number of bottles of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinches' and 'bottles' both look like the thief's verb and the loot; bottles is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse was a German-born novelist, author of Siddhartha and Steppenwolf, who won the Nobel Prize in 1946.
